statement: The first line holds n and k; the second holds n integers, negatives allowed. Print the length of the longest contiguous subarray summing to exactly k, or 0 when none exists. Walk once carrying the running prefix sum and a map from each prefix value to the first index where it appeared (seed: prefix 0 at index -1). At index i, if prefix minus k was first seen at j, the subarray j+1 to i sums to k - track the widest such gap. First occurrences only: overwriting shrinks the gap.

example.why: The whole array sums to 2: prefix 2 at the end minus the seeded prefix 0 at index -1.

hint: Store a prefix's index only on first sight - the earliest marker gives the longest span.
mistake: Reaching for the sliding window; negatives break its grow-shrink logic, prefixes are immune.
